{'id': '0', 'translation': "Chief Executive John Lee today attended the first 'dialogue and exchange session' at the Legislative Council, and met with the media after the meeting alongside Legislative Council President Starry Lee. In response to the long-term housing arrangements for Wang Fuk Court, Lee stated that 53% of owners have signed sale agreements, and urged residents to 'make their decisions promptly.' He also addressed the early retirement of Judge Justin Chan Ka-shun over alleged judicial plagiarism, saying he respects the Chief Justice's appropriate measures to maintain public confidence in the independent and professional fulfilment of judicial duties. Regarding the vacant seat left by Wong Kam-fai's resignation over drunk driving charges, Lee noted that three important elections will be held in the next 18 months, and that priority should be given to these three elections in terms of timing, workload and relative necessity."}

{'id': '1', 'translation': "Chief Executive John Lee attended a 'dialogue and exchange session' at the Legislative Council today and responded to media questions afterwards."}

{'id': '2', 'translation': '53% of owners sign sale agreements; nearly 91% sign acquisition letters'}

{'id': '3', 'translation': "When asked about the acquisition of Wang Fuk Court and whether he had inquired about the reasons why some residents had not signed consent forms, Lee said the matter has been handled with 'compassion, reason and the law' throughout. He reiterated that regarding long-term housing arrangements, the government is acquiring ownership at a price of HK$8,000 to HK$10,500 per square foot, and is bearing various risks, including uncertainties over insurance compensation and potential legal proceedings."}

{'id': '4', 'translation': "He said that as of yesterday, 90.8% of owners had signed letters accepting the acquisition proposal and 53% had completed signing sale agreements, with some owners having formally completed title transfers. He described the process as smooth and urged 'everyone to make decisions promptly.' He noted that while the decision must be made by each household based on its own circumstances, regarding the acquisition price, risk-bearing and other assistance, 'we hope to allow the relevant households to make decisions as soon as possible, so that everyone can resume normal life at an early date.' He also mentioned that units would soon be released for residents to consider: 'Seize this opportunity early — you may be able to apply for the long-term housing unit of your choice.'"}

{'id': '5', 'translation': "Lee reiterated that the government has recently optimised the rent subsidy arrangement, and the Legislative Council's funding application of HK$1 billion for the acquisition of Wang Chi Court has been approved. He said the government will continue its explanatory work and that residents with questions or requests can relay them to the explanation team or the one-social-worker-per-household scheme, adding that matters will be handled flexibly and pragmatically according to actual circumstances."}

{'id': '6', 'translation': 'Asked about the long-term housing arrangements for Wang Fuk Court, Lee said 53% of owners have signed sale agreements, and some owners have completed title transfers, describing the process as smooth.'}

{'id': '7', 'translation': "Response on Chan Ka-shun's plagiarism and early retirement: respect for the Chief Justice's appropriate measures"}

{'id': '8', 'translation': "As for High Court judge of the Court of First Instance Justin Chan Ka-shun, who was found to have plagiarised on multiple occasions and was required by Chief Justice Andrew Cheung yesterday to retire early, Lee was asked whether this was sufficient to restore public confidence. Lee stated that society has high expectations of judges and professional standards, and that the judiciary has consistently operated and managed independently. He said he respects the Chief Justice's appropriate measures to maintain public confidence in the independent and professional fulfilment of judicial duties, and expressed confidence that judges and judicial officers at all levels will abide by the judicial oath and perform their duties with diligence, independence and professionalism."}

{'id': '9', 'translation': "High Court judge Justin Chan Ka-shun, involved in alleged judicial plagiarism, was required to retire early. The Chief Executive responded today that he respects the Chief Justice's appropriate measures to maintain public confidence. (File photo)"}

{'id': '10', 'translation': "Separately, University of Hong Kong (HKU) President Zhang Xiang, who was previously embroiled in a campus governance controversy, announced yesterday that he will step down in 2028 after completing two terms totalling ten years. Asked how he would evaluate Zhang's performance and whether he would require HKU to include terms requiring better communication with the Council when hiring a new president, Lee said Zhang is a scientist passionate about science who is eager to return to the laboratory to solve scientific problems and contribute to society. He thanked Zhang for giving early notice of his decision to the Council, allowing the university sufficient time to recruit a new president."}

{'id': '11', 'translation': "Lee also thanked Zhang for his past and future contributions while serving as president, and his diligent work for HKU. He said the appointment of the president would be handled by the Council, noting that universities have well-functioning mechanisms for hiring presidents. He expressed confidence in the Council's handling of the matter, and believes it can ensure the new president leads HKU in sustained development and continuous progress."}

{'id': '12', 'translation': "HKU President Zhang Xiang announced yesterday he will step down in 2028. Lee thanked him for his contributions to HKU and expressed confidence in the Council's recruitment work. (File photo)"}

{'id': '13', 'translation': "No by-election for Wong Kam-fai's resignation: priority given to three upcoming elections"}

{'id': '14', 'translation': 'Legislative Council member Wong Kam-fai was arrested for drunk driving late last month and resigned earlier this month, drawing public attention to whether a by-election would be held. Secretary for Constitutional and Mainland Affairs Alice Mak had earlier indicated the timing was tight. When asked again today about the by-election, Lee noted that three important elections will be held in the next 18 months: the Election Committee election in November this year, the Chief Executive election in March next year, and the District Council election before the end of next year. He said that for any election, the Electoral Affairs Commission (EAC) will consider a combination of factors, including manpower resources, venue arrangements, polling station setup, and the procurement and transport of election supplies, and must assess the overall work arrangements and relative necessity of each election based on actual circumstances.'}

{'id': '15', 'translation': "Lee added that after the Election Committee election is completed in November this year, it will take office on February 1 next year to perform its role in the relevant elections. He said he felt that 'compared with a by-election for a single vacancy in the Legislative Council, in terms of timing, workload and relative necessity, these three elections should be prioritised.'"}

{'id': '16', 'translation': "Following Wong Kam-fai's resignation over drunk driving charges, attention is focused on whether a by-election will be held for the vacancy. Lee said the three upcoming elections should be prioritised, while Legislative Council President Starry Lee said she respects the Chief Executive's and the EAC's assessment."}

{'id': '17', 'translation': "Asked whether the reduction in members would affect the Council's work and whether she had spoken with Xia Baolong, Starry Lee said she understands and respects the assessments of the Chief Executive and the EAC, and that as an important working partner of the government, the Legislative Council will certainly lend its support to a series of important initiatives, including the first Five-Year Plan and the Policy Address. She continued that while there have been changes in the Council with only 89 members remaining, 'I believe every member understands that we need to step up, support one another and share the burden, given the new situation arising from this unforeseeable change.' She said all members will give their full effort, and that with 89 members working together, the Council can continue to perform its functions as always."}

{'id': '18', 'translation': 'No response on whether Huanggang Port will open before 1 October'}

{'id': '19', 'translation': "The legislative proposal for the Hong Kong port area of the new Huanggang Port was passed earlier by the Legislative Council, and together with related subsidiary legislation will take effect on 31 July, although the official opening date has not been announced. Asked whether the port could be formally opened before 1 October, Lee did not give a direct answer but said he understood the public's keen interest in the port. He said that after the Hong Kong port area is established on 31 July, the governments of Hong Kong and Shenzhen will carry out operational testing on the port's operation, including work on system, equipment and traffic stress tests. He emphasised that the installation of equipment and facilities, operational testing and drills are being advanced at full speed, with the goal of completing them as soon as possible so the facility can be opened to the public, adding that any decisions will be announced."}
